problem_statement: Simply Docs is a runnable static documentation / blog template (built on Simple.css) for a small open-source project. It spans a Home page, a Documentation page, a News page, a Blog Post page and an Author page, all sharing one header/navigation/footer chrome. The Documentation page ships several reference and guide sections (two API-route references, a code-snippets guide, an editing & theming guide, a Markdown example and a syntax-highlighting example) but offers no way to narrow the page to one kind of section — a reader who only wants the API reference has to scroll past everything. Add the docs site's own native section filter: a "Filter docs by section" control at the top of the Documentation page's section grid, with pills for All / Reference / Guides / Examples (each showing its count), a live readout of the form "Showing N of 6 · <section>", and a card grid of the six doc sections tagged by section. Clicking a pill must filter the visible section cards, mark the clicked pill active, and update both the count and the readout to match the shown cards. The filter control must be laid out responsively (its pill row wraps instead of overflowing on a 390px phone) and the section cards must stay legible and non-overlapping. Also surface a shared "Docs quick-nav" rail (links into the documentation, syntax-highlighting and Markdown sections, the release news and the maintainer page) in the footer region of the Home, Documentation and News pages so the docs navigation is reachable across the site. Keep the existing Simple.css visual system, the header navigation, the footer and every page's content and routes intact.
required_content: Add a "Filter docs by section" control at the top of the Documentation page's section grid, with pills for All / Reference / Guides / Examples (each showing its section count) and a live readout of the form "Showing N of 6 · <section>".

Render the six documentation sections (two API-route references, a code-snippets guide, an editing & theming guide, a Markdown example and a syntax-highlighting example) as a grid of cards, each tagged with its section (Reference / Guides / Examples).

Clicking a section pill must filter the visible cards to that section, mark the clicked pill active, and update the count and the readout to match the shown cards (e.g. clicking Reference shows "Showing 2 of 6 · Reference").
The filter pill row must wrap (not overflow the viewport) at 390px mobile and 834px tablet, and the section cards must remain legible and non-overlapping at every breakpoint.

Surface a shared "Docs quick-nav" rail in the footer region of the Home, Documentation and News pages, linking into the documentation, syntax-highlighting and Markdown sections, the release news and the maintainer page.
Keep the existing Simple.css visual system, the header navigation, the footer and every page's content and routes intact.
design_constraints: Realize the section filter and the Docs quick-nav rail as the docs site's own native navigation, styled with the existing Simple.css tokens (accent #0d47a1, accent-bg #f5f7ff, border tokens); do not introduce a foreign visual system.
The filter must be keyboard- and pointer-operable buttons; clicking a pill re-filters the card grid client-side without a page reload and keeps the readout in sync with the shown cards.
The pill row must be responsive (wrap on narrow viewports) and the card grid must not overlap/shingle or drop below the contrast needed to read the card titles and body text.
The Docs quick-nav rail is a shared component; it must appear in the footer region of the Home, Documentation and News pages so docs navigation is consistent across the site.
Preserve the Home/Documentation/News/Blog Post/Author routes, the header navigation, the footer and all existing page content byte-for-byte outside the added filter, grid and rail.
author_notes: Add the Simply Docs template's own native section filter to the Documentation page: a "Filter docs by section" pill bar (All / Reference / Guides / Examples with counts) over a responsive grid of six section cards (API references, guides and examples), plus a live "Showing N of 6" readout, and a shared Docs quick-nav rail in the footer of Home, Documentation and News. The filter re-renders the section cards and the readout on click; the grid image/card layout must stay legible and must not overflow the 390px mobile viewport. Style everything with the existing Simple.css accent palette and keep the favicon/OG image assets and all routes intact.

change_completion: The Documentation page shows the Filter docs by section control with All / Reference / Guides / Examples pills (each with its count) over a grid of the six section cards, plus a live Showing N of 6 readout.

Clicking a section pill filters the visible cards, marks that pill active, and advances the count and readout to match the shown cards (clicking Reference reads Showing 2 of 6 Reference), and the shared Docs quick-nav rail is present on Home, Documentation and News.
design_consistency: The section filter and Docs quick-nav rail read as a coherent Simple.css docs design (accent #0d47a1, accent-bg #f5f7ff panels, restrained typography) with legible card titles and body text.
The filtered card grid is not shingled/overlapping and the pills and card text are not rendered as low-contrast near-white-on-near-white or into an unrelated design language.
responsive: Desktop, tablet and 390px mobile states of the Documentation page have no horizontal overflow, and the filter pill row wraps instead of overflowing.
Mobile keeps the section cards readable in a wrapped single-column rhythm with tappable pills.
regression: The original header navigation, footer, page routes and the Home / Documentation / News / Author content remain visible, and the documentation TOC and section headings are preserved.
Bundled assets assets/images/headshot.jpg (and favicon/OG image) remain browser-visible and no remote media or new dependencies are introduced.

state_constraints: desktop_home, tablet_home and mobile_home verify the Home page loads across breakpoints with no horizontal overflow and carries the shared Docs quick-nav rail.

mobile_docs and tablet_docs verify the section filter pill row wraps and fits the phone/tablet with no horizontal overflow; the original-with-defect leg overflows about 271px on mobile and a shallow non-fix still overflows about 291px.

desktop_docs and mobile_docs verify the filtered section-card grid keeps the Simple.css visual language and reads as legible, non-overlapping cards, not a shingled illegible near-white-on-near-white pile.

docs_filter verifies the section filter's readout and count advance to Showing 2 of 6 Reference after the Reference pill is clicked (interaction continuity), changed from the pre-click desktop_docs state.
desktop_home, desktop_docs and desktop_news verify the shared Docs quick-nav rail is present across the site, not only on Home (cross-page design continuity).
desktop_author verifies the local maintainer headshot (assets/images/headshot.jpg) remains browser-visible after the change.
